sources.title: Optum advances digital prior authorization
sources.supports: Humata deployment claim and Allina planned deployment, not UHG cohort

financial_anchor.caveat: FY affected by elevated medical cost, restructuring and other items; Q2 2026 OP was $8.0bn.

ai_claim.claim: Optum markets authorization technology; 96% first-pass refers to Humata deployments, while >25% reauthorization reduction was policy removal rather than AI.
ai_claim.stage: E1; at most limited E2 for third-party Humata deployments, not UHG cohort
ai_claim.limitation: No company-specific production outcome, independent non-inferiority or cash reconciliation.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: FY2025 medical-care ratio rose to 88.9%, while litigation disputes automated denial use.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Aggregate result is not a causal AI test; allegations unresolved.

rights_limit: HIPAA, contracts and purpose limits govern claims/clinical data; cross-customer training and naviHealth decision rights are not public.
materiality_summary: 5% of exact FY2025 operating earnings $18.964bn is $948.2m annual pre-tax.

arithmetic.inputs: assumed $8bn eligible admin cost, 15% efficiency, 50% realization, 50% retention, $250m run cost

g2_provisional: Insufficient: E1 product and limited third-party Humata deployment evidence lack a company-specific controlled quality/cash cohort.
